description: Fig. 1 is a single-panel schematic diagram — no axes, no scale bar, no printed numbers — that illustrates how indentation testing is used to evaluate fracture toughness. On a light blue-grey background sits a grey, diamond-shaped indentation impression drawn with concentric shading; a yellow arrow labelled "Indentation" points to it. Four thin dark cracks radiate from the four corners of the indent (top, bottom, left, right), the classic indentation crack pattern produced by a sharp (Vickers-type) pyramidal indenter; a second yellow arrow labelled "Crack" points to the upper radial crack. To the right of the indent a yellow double-headed arrow spans from the right indent corner to the tip of the right-hand radial crack; this span is labelled l_i (italic l with subscript i), i.e. the crack length that enters indentation fracture-toughness formulae. No measured value — no hardness, applied load, toughness or length in µm — is printed anywhere on the panel. The figure's argument is procedural: a sharp indenter generates a controlled diamond impression plus well-defined radial cracks, and the crack length l_i, not a bulk specimen test, is the measurable input for fracture-toughness evaluation.

subfigures.description: Schematic of an indentation fracture-toughness test: a grey diamond-shaped indent with four radial corner cracks on a light blue-grey field, annotated with yellow arrows and text 'Indentation' and 'Crack', and a yellow double-headed arrow labelled l_i measuring the crack length from the indent corner to the crack tip on the right.

observations.observation: The figure is a schematic drawing, not a micrograph or data plot: it has a uniform light blue-grey background with no axes, tick marks or scale bar.
A grey diamond-shaped indentation impression is at the centre, rendered with concentric grey shading that gives it a dished/tensile appearance.
A yellow arrow with the word 'Indentation' points diagonally down-right at the diamond indent.
Four radial cracks (thin dark lines) emanate from the four corners of the indent in the vertical and horizontal directions.
A yellow arrow with the word 'Crack' points left at the crack above the indent.
A yellow double-headed horizontal arrow to the right of the indent spans from the right indent corner to the tip of the right-hand crack and is labelled l_i (italic l with subscript i).
No numeric values, units, magnification or scale bar are printed on the panel.
The caption states the figure is a schematic diagram demonstrating the approach to evaluating fracture toughness using indentation techniques.
The green/grey shading gradient inside the diamond indent is a purely illustrative rendering and carries no quantitative information.
